title: Unknowable Uncertainty
hook: Your five-year forecast is a guess dressed up in a spreadsheet. Some things just can't be predicted.
statement: When the odds are truly unknowable, stop trying to predict and start running experiments.
explainer: In a brand new market there's no real data to forecast from. Your job is to survive being wrong. Keep each bet small enough to lose, keep options open, and learn fast.
sop: Write down what you truly can't know yet.
Set an affordable loss for each bet.
Run several small experiments at once.
Update your beliefs from real evidence.
Put more behind the early winners.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Affordable Loss 8, Optionality 6, Learning Rate 7. (8 + 6 + 7) ÷ 3 = 7.0. Higher means you can be wrong a lot and still learn. Lower means one bad bet could end things before you learn anything.
question: Pick one thing you're trying to predict and write a small test you could run instead.
closing_statement: You can't forecast uncertainty. You can only survive it.
caption:
Principle Nº 305: Unknowable Uncertainty

Your five-year forecast is a guess dressed up in a spreadsheet. Some things just can't be predicted.

When the odds are truly unknowable, stop trying to predict and start running experiments.

Your turn: Pick one thing you're trying to predict and write a small test you could run instead.
